answer: Scoped attestation mirroring. Each agent identity must accumulate a history of co-signed task receipts from independent counterparties, and the protocol stores a mirror of those counterparties' own receipt graphs. To register, an attacker must recruit real distinct counterparties whose histories anchor into the existing graph, since self-generated clusters fail the cross-check. Cost: acquiring N genuine counterparties with non-overlapping histories, plus latency and coordination per identity. A cedar-like growth constraint caps receipts per counterparty pair, forcing breadth over depth.
